exposure: history of obstetrics complications (e.g., prolonged labor)
cohort: The study participants were 2661 clients from Nekemte Specialized Hospital in Oromia Regional State, Western Ethiopia, whose data from January 2014 to December 2022 were systematically sampled and reviewed.
finding: The trend of uterine rupture declined from 1.54% in 2014 to 0.93% in 2022, with an overall prevalence of 3.53%, and was significantly associated with low household income, grandmultiparity, history of prolonged labor, history of cesarean section, and history of uterine repair.
mod_finding: A history of cesarean section was identified as a significant factor associated with uterine rupture.
cross-section timing: The study analyzed data collected between January 2014 and December 2022, with data extraction performed from March 2023 to August 2023.
